title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1968-06-14

ai_review.summary: Rare early St. Stephen show with smoking The Eleven and powerful Jerry, but hampered by a ragged audience recording.
ai_review.review: This 1968 performance is prized for its historic early St. Stephen sequence, a smoking The Eleven segue, and an inspired lead from Jerry Garcia that lifts the entire set despite the low‑fidelity tape. Reviewers note the unusual feedback sandwich opening/closing and quirky transitions (Alligator → Lovelight), while repeatedly calling out the poor audio quality – clipping, muffled vocals and overall raggedness – as a drawback that can be endured with good headphones.

ai_rating.rationale: Show is consistently praised (standout performances, high energy) while recording quality is uniformly described as poor/fair; weighting the strong show (≈4.5) against weak audio (≈2) yields a combined rating around 3.8.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Audio is ragged with clipping, barely audible vocals and low‑fidelity sound; however some reviewers find it listenable on headphones despite the noise.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Features a rare feedback sandwich (opening and closing with feedback) and unusual segues such as feedback → The Eleven → St. Stephen and Alligator → Lovelight; overall flow is unique but can feel disjointed due to tape quirks.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia's lead guitar and vocal performance are highlighted as exceptional, carrying the show even through poor sound quality.
band_member_comments.Phil: Occasional bass fills are noted, adding depth to the performance.
